scope: Primary-source review of cold KV compression, tiered retention, paused agent sessions, and integration prior art. Sources are grouped by project or research method.
conclusion: Substantial direct prior art exists. A causal policy/evaluation experiment is justified; unique technical novelty, customer demand, and end-to-end performance advantage are not established.

verification.method: Read primary papers and abstracts, official documentation, public RFCs, author repositories, and selected raw LMCache source through web tools.
verification.date_convention: publication_date is the first paper submission or issue opening date when verified. Null denotes an undated rolling source; accessed_at is not its release date.
verification.license_convention: Code licenses are distinct from paper licenses. Null means unverified in this review, not absent or unavailable. Repository-level evidence does not settle every dependency or file license.
verification.maturity_convention: Documented implementation, experimental implementation, research paper, open RFC, and small prototype are separate evidence categories. None means independently benchmarked here.
limitations: Rolling documentation and dev/main branches can change. Pin immutable revisions before integration or benchmark comparisons.
Reported results belong to the cited authors and vendors and cannot be used as measured KVpilot performance.
This is not an exhaustive novelty, patent, or freedom-to-operate search.

sources.title: LMCache MP storage, serde, lazy offload, and policy extension surfaces

code.license_evidence: Repository license declaration and SPDX headers in inspected raw source.
code.inspection: Store/prefetch policies and serde exports/factory inspected; complete TurboQuant kernels and concurrency behavior not audited.

findings: MP exposes custom store/prefetch policies, configurable L1/L2 eviction, FP8 and TurboQuant L2 serde, and eviction-aware lazy offload.
Store target selection can omit keys; default and skip_l1 store policies and default/retain prefetch policies already exist.
MP policy choices differ from legacy policy choices; runtime subprocess plugins are distinct from synchronous serde hooks.
limits: Documented L2 serde does not itself establish compression before GPU-to-host transfer.
Exact released engine/connector compatibility and actual codec performance remain unverified.
sources.relevance: Existing integration platform and mandatory baseline, not evidence of an empty codec/policy market.

sources.title: CacheGen: KV Cache Compression and Streaming for Fast Large Language Model Serving

code.license_evidence: Author-linked repository; standalone repository license not verified. LMCache integration has separate project license evidence.
code.inspection: Paper and integration documentation; implementation not reproduced.

findings: Combines distribution-aware KV encoding and streaming with bandwidth-adaptive compression choices.
limits: Paper results depend on its models, network conditions, and quality criteria.
Legacy remote_serde configuration is not automatically the current MP integration API.
sources.relevance: Direct prior art against claiming bandwidth-adaptive KV compression is new.

sources.title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion

code.license_evidence: Code linked by authors; license not verified in this review.
code.inspection: Paper and LMCache FAQ; target-engine implementation not run.

findings: Selectively recomputes attention dependencies when reusing non-prefix context chunks.
limits: Context fusion is different from exact prefix persistence.
LMCache FAQ qualifies latest-vLLM availability; verify a concrete compatible release with maintainers.
sources.relevance: Adjacent reuse baseline; prevents treating arbitrary concatenated cached contexts as semantically equivalent.

sources.title: CacheFocus

code.license_evidence: Author-maintained implementation and license not verified.

findings: Uses offline RAG caching, positional adjustment, and adaptive pruning/allocation.
limits: RAG benchmark results do not establish arbitrary multi-turn branch replay safety.
sources.relevance: Adjacent RAG/context reuse work, not a general reversible cold-cache codec.

sources.title: CacheFlow: Efficient LLM Serving with 3D-Parallel KV Cache Restoration

code.license_evidence: Author-maintained code and license not verified.

findings: Schedules restoration and recomputation across token, layer, and GPU dimensions with batch-aware contention considerations.
limits: Must reproduce scheduling and resource overlap before transferring results to another engine.
Distinct from the video-generation CacheFlow paper and historical company naming.
sources.relevance: Prior art for treating cache restoration as a scheduling problem, beyond compression ratio.

sources.title: Fast KV Compaction via Attention Matching

code.inspection: Paper, author repository, and separate Baseten experiment; no reproduction here.

findings: Fits compact K/V and attention-mass biases to reference queries; it changes the attended representation rather than merely encoding bytes.
Baseten separately reports repeated-compaction degradation in its tested setting, with differences from the original implementation.
limits: Quality and fitting cost depend on task/method; extreme reported compression is not universal.
Does not establish 128k coding-agent correctness, ready-made vLLM integration, or proportional concurrency gains.
sources.relevance: Potential later semantic-compression comparator; too complex to use as a first CPU storage-codec baseline.

sources.title: TurboQuant

code.license_evidence: LMCache repository/license headers; this is not a verified license for an original Google implementation.
code.inspection: Paper, Google Research article dated 2026-03-24, and LMCache serde documentation/exports.

findings: Low-bit rotation-based quantization is already available as an LMCache storage option.
limits: Effective bit rate must include metadata and alignment.
Attention-logit kernel results cannot be read as end-to-end server throughput or multi-agent concurrency.
sources.relevance: Mandatory practical low-bit comparator; not a novel codec contribution of KVpilot.

sources.title: KV Cache Transform Coding for Compact Storage in LLM Inference

code.license_evidence: An official author-maintained implementation/license was not verified; similarly named third-party repositories are not treated as author evidence.
code.inspection: Paper and author-associated SGLang API proposal.

findings: Combines PCA feature decorrelation, adaptive quantization, and entropy coding with initial calibration.
Explicitly targets reusable chat and iterative-code caches, including cold storage and restoration.
limits: Reconstructed full KV still consumes active cache space.
Reported high compression varies by use case and is not a measured controller benefit.
sources.relevance: Very close prior art to the original latent/low-rank cold-cache pitch.

sources.title: KVCodec: Efficient Remote KV Cache Reuse with GPU-native Video Codec

code.license_evidence: Author-maintained implementation and license not verified.
code.inspection: Latest primary paper metadata and method.

findings: Uses codec-friendly layouts and GPU video codec engines with transfer/decode/restoration pipelining.
limits: Hardware availability and simultaneous model execution affect any advantage.
CPU synthetic codec measurements cannot validate this implementation's hardware overlap.
sources.relevance: Prior art for reducing codec compute contention while compressing remote caches.

sources.title: KVzip: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression with Context Reconstruction

code.inspection: Paper, project page, and repository documentation; no model execution.

findings: Uses context reconstruction to score KV for query-agnostic pruning and multi-query reuse.
The authors also list a later FastKVzip project.
limits: Scoring work adds prefill cost; optimized kernel support varies by model.
Logical token savings alone do not prove runtime acceleration.
sources.relevance: Strong comparator when proposing reusable semantic cache reduction.

sources.title: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling

code.license_evidence: Repository inspected but license not verified.
code.inspection: Paper and repository documentation; original Zefan-Cai URL redirects to this repository.

findings: Allocates different KV token budgets across model layers.
limits: Token eviction is irreversible information removal.
Long-context benchmark quality does not establish repeated paused-session reliability.
sources.relevance: Established token-selection baseline rather than a reversible storage codec.

sources.title: VarRate: Training-Free Variable-Rate KV Cache Compression for Long-Context LLMs

code.license_evidence: Author code and license not verified.

findings: Allocates variable nonzero low-rank budgets using query salience, with query-agnostic reuse comparisons.
limits: Retaining a representation of every token is not lossless preservation.
Model/task coverage and production kernels need independent validation.
sources.relevance: Adaptive representation allocation already has direct contemporary research prior art.

sources.title: Read What Matters: Query-Adaptive Quantization for KV Caches

code.license_evidence: Author code and license not verified.

findings: Stores immutable progressive codes and varies key/value precision fetched per query.
Separates retained-capacity budget from per-query read budget.
limits: The reported latency experiment uses an 8K-token, batch-one, single-layer A10G workload.
This is not proof of full-engine serving or paused-session transfer performance.
sources.relevance: Useful precision/provenance design comparator; not a demonstrated replacement for a cold-store controller.

sources.title: KV Cache Compression in TensorRT-LLM: cold-page NVFP4

code.license_evidence: Repository LICENSE includes multiple component licenses; exact cold-page file license not independently resolved in this review.
code.revision: rolling documentation; release and commit unpinned
code.inspection: Official technical article with implementation paths; kernels not independently audited or run.

findings: Fuses cold-page NVFP4 quantization/offload and dequantization/reload.
Documents idempotent round trips for its specific representation after initial quantization, with vendor quality/performance tests.
limits: Representation-specific idempotence is not a guarantee for Attention Matching or arbitrary codecs.
Hardware, supported cache kinds, release compatibility, and real workload results require reproduction.
sources.relevance: Direct implemented overlap with compress-before-offload; mandatory competitor for product positioning.

sources.title: Adaptive KV Retention for LLM Agents at Human-Approval Timescales

code.license_evidence: Author implementation and license not verified.

findings: Studies long human-approval waits with opportunity-cost-aware retention and load-dependent expiration.
Uses aggregate wait calibration rather than requiring exact per-request future wait predictions.
limits: No independent reproduction or customer deployment verification in this review.
sources.relevance: Closest policy/economics prior art; a proposed KVpilot policy must compare against it or clearly state why it cannot.

sources.title: vLLM Programmable KV Cache RFC and SGLang KV Cache Compression API RFC
sources.date_basis: vLLM issue opening and SGLang issue opening, respectively

code.license_evidence: Issues are design proposals. No specific merged implementation or proposal-derived code is bundled here.
code.inspection: RFC text and issue status; SGLang proposal names v0.5.18 as its base.

findings: vLLM proposal distinguishes lifecycle associations, physical residency, references, and completed operations for branching agents.
SGLang proposes extensible HostKVCache codecs, positional metadata, page state, and streaming layer loads.
limits: Open issue text does not establish supported released APIs.
Detailed compatibility, cancellation, synchronization, and resource approval must be implemented and tested.
sources.relevance: Avoid inventing a parallel lifecycle protocol before checking upstream direction and concrete merged interfaces.

sources.title: Dynamo ThunderAgent Program Scheduler

code.inspection: Official experimental feature documentation and repository license; not run.

findings: Program-aware admission and placement model acting/reasoning and active/paused states.
Logical pauses occur at tool boundaries and use guaranteed GPU/host capacity in scheduling.
limits: Experimental status; pause is not arbitrary decode preemption.
Scheduling capability is distinct from a measured adaptive codec selector.
sources.relevance: Existing agent lifecycle scheduling work and potential integration context.

sources.title: kvpolicy: quantized KV-cache persistence for local LLM agents

code.inspection: Repository description/license; detailed code and claimed benchmarks not reproduced.

findings: A small public project already targets quantized local-agent session persistence and resumption.
limits: README performance claims are self-reported and not treated as verified results.
Production compatibility, workload coverage, and policy behavior were not audited.
sources.relevance: Direct small-prototype prior art; prevents presenting local quantized session save/resume as an untouched niche.
